report.tagline: An Indian app to book trained, verified professionals for salon at home, cleaning, repairs and house help, at fixed prices.
report.simpleSummary: Urban Company is an app where you book someone to come to your home: a beautician, an AC repair technician, a plumber, a cleaner, or a house helper in 15 minutes through InstaHelp. You see a fixed price before booking, pay in the app, and rate the person after. Urban Company trains and checks the professionals, gives them tools and products, and takes a cut of each job. It also sells its own Native water purifiers and smart locks, and runs in the UAE and Saudi Arabia.

overview.whatItDoes: Urban Company is a marketplace that connects households with tens of thousands of independent service professionals. Unlike a listings site, it controls quality: it trains partners, sets prices, supplies products and handles payment and complaints. It earns a commission from each job, plus margin on its own Native products.
howItWorks: The customer picks a service, like a ₹1,000 salon package or AC service, and chooses a time slot.
The app assigns a trained partner near the customer; the partner accepts the job.
The partner arrives with Urban Company kits and products, does the job and the customer pays in the app.
Urban Company keeps a commission and the partner gets the rest; partners also buy products and training from it.
Ratings after each job decide which partners get more work; low-rated partners get retrained or removed.
InstaHelp sends a house helper for cleaning, dishes or laundry in about 15 minutes, paid by the hour.
overview.valueProposition: For customers: a reliable, safe, fixed-price professional at home, with a re-do or refund if something goes wrong. For partners: steady jobs and higher earnings than working alone.

businessModel.summary: Urban Company makes money by taking a commission on each service job, selling products and training to partners, selling its own Native devices, and membership fees. The core India services business is now profitable, but the company as a whole loses money because it is spending heavily to grow InstaHelp.

revenueStreams.detail: A cut of each booking, often estimated at around 20% to 30% depending on category.
Partners buy salon products and tools from Urban Company.
Water purifiers and smart locks; ₹105 crore net revenue in Q2 FY27.
Hourly house help; ₹71 crore NTV in Q2 FY27, still loss-making.
UAE and Saudi Arabia; ₹75 crore net revenue in Q2 FY27.

businessModel.pricing: Fixed prices shown in the app by service and city. Example: AC service and salon packages from a few hundred to a few thousand rupees. InstaHelp is charged by the hour, with low introductory prices. UC Plus membership is a paid plan with discounts.
costDrivers: InstaHelp helper pay guarantees during low demand
Cost of Native products and installation
businessModel.unitEconomics: On a ₹1,000 salon booking, the partner keeps roughly ₹750 to ₹800 and Urban Company keeps about ₹200 to ₹250 as commission. After payment fees, support, marketing and discounts, it earns only a small profit; the core India business had an adjusted EBITDA margin of 3.5% of NTV in Q2 FY27, about ₹35 on that ₹1,000. InstaHelp loses about ₹279 per order, because hourly prices are low and helpers are paid even when idle. It only works if helpers get booked back to back in each neighbourhood.

growth.moat: The moat is the trained supply base. Building thousands of skilled, vetted partners in each city with standard kits and training takes years. A new app can copy the booking screen, but not the quality and trust. InstaHelp has a weaker moat because cleaning needs less skill, which is why Snabbit and Pronto could enter fast.

pmLessons: In service marketplaces, supply quality is the product. Urban Company wins by training and controlling partners, not just matching them.
A two-sided marketplace must keep both sides happy. Squeezing partners for margin leads to protests and worse service.
A high-frequency service like InstaHelp can build habit, but it must find a path to profit per order.
Fixed prices remove a big source of anxiety in Indian home services.

interviewQuestions.question: InstaHelp loses ₹279 per order. How would you get it to break even?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break the loss into price, helper pay, idle time and marketing. Ideas: density in fewer areas, subscriptions, peak pricing. Pick guardrails for quality.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce partner cancellations?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find causes (travel, better jobs, fatigue). Fixes: smarter routing, cancellation penalties with fairness, backup pool. Measure cancellation rate.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Urban Company's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Good-quality jobs completed. Explain why not revenue. Break into demand, supply, quality.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Urban Company enter tier-3 cities?
interviewQuestions.hint: Consider price sensitivity, partner supply, density needed for unit economics. Start with high-margin categories.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to increase trust for first-time customers.
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona: worried about safety and price. Ideas: partner profile video, live tracking, guarantee badge. Measure first-to-second booking rate.
